title: Leaving Rice; Dakota tours; Burke Bailey suggests Milwaukee
summary: Thomas lists Rice sidemen. After touring the Dakotas, Iowa and Nebraska, he left Minneapolis for Milwaukee on tenor saxophonist Burke Bailey's advice.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Well, when you leave him, he says then you were with a trombonist called Shuffle Abernathy? Is that right?

Yes, that's right. Well, you see there were some business deals. I don't know what happened because /I wasn't in on the business deals so we had built a pretty rugged band there and we used to, lot of
guys like George E. Lee and Benny Moten in Sioux City, Iowa.

Yeah, we're out of Minneapolis. We played the Dakotas, we played North and South Dakota, Iowa, Nebraska, see what I mean? ... all those bands, you know. So, it got out of hand. I didn't see anything was happening there so I decided to risk making it. So I went to Milwaukee. Oh, Burke Bailey, I must tell you about Burke Bailey. Burke Bailey I always thought he was a tremendous musician and lot of things I don't think happened TO Burke Bailey. Another fellow by the name of Norman Mason So, I who decided to go to Milwaukee. I talked to Burke about it.
Norman Mason I met him later. I'll tell you about him.
And they were in the Eli Rice band?

No, no. Burke Bailey was in the Rice band. So, he suggested Milwaukee. So we go to Milwaukee, we got there around this time of year, you know, ... so a fellow was getting a band together, a fellow by the name of Shuffle Abernathy. So, out in that part of the country people don't ... venture there out that way. When a musician pass through, they want you in there if you can make it. It's tremendous. He had a little band out there.
